title: Chapter 22. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — VI: the wedding with Vishnupriya; the beginning of the ashtakaliya
html:
Continuation of the appendix (the introductory note on the two Naraharis, on the arguments for attribution and on the marks in the headings is in ch. 17). Chapter 22: the end of GPT section 2.4 "The second marriage" — the wedding procession to the house of Sanatana Mishra, the reception of the bridegroom, the wedding, the gods and celestial women at the wedding, the bridal chamber (vasara), the morning after the wedding and the Lord's return home with Vishnupriya (nos. 1–16; GPT 2.4 nos. 18–20, 22–34); the beginning of section 5.2 "Ashtakaliya" — the songs of Gaura's awakening at the end of the night (nos. 17–26; GPT 5.2 nos. 1–10). Narahari Chakravarti quotes all the wedding padas of the chapter one after another in the 12th wave of the Bhakti-ratnakara (Ishana shows Srinivasa the house of Jagannatha Mishra), and all the awakening songs in his Gaura-charita-chintamani (kiranas 2–3: the last part of the night and the awakening). Before translation the signatures in these sections were checked throughout, in the OCR and on the scan; the Bhakti-ratnakara (ed. 1960, vv. 1491–1626) was read continuously. Not translated: 2.4 no. 17 — signed Ghanashyama (outside the appendix); no. 21 — a pada in nagari-bhava (assigned to the section of nagari padas); nos. 35–38 — without the Narahari signature: an extract from Lochana Dasa's Chaitanya-mangala (no. 38 is signed "dāsa trilocana"; translated with Lochana, Chaitanya-mangala, Adi-khanda, part 14, vv. ≈146–178); nos. 39–40 — Vrindavana Dasa (= CB Adi 15). The base text is GPT1 (doubtful places from the scan), collated with GPT2, the BR (eds. 1912 and 1960) and the Gaura-charita-chintamani (ed. 1947); PK, KGC, PS and the Gita-chandrodaya have been checked. On Vishnupriya and the wedding rites as lila see note 2; on the motif of the women of Nadia, note 5; on the ashtakaliya as eternal lila, note 36. The notes of the GPT editors are not reproduced.

1. Narahari — "gaura rasika-śekharabara…" (GPT1 p. 100, section 2.4, no. 18; BR)

The wedding procession: Gaura, surrounded by brahmanas, sets out for the wedding in a palanquin; instruments of the four kinds sound; invisible celestial dancers dance together with earthly ones, the gandharvas sing with the singers; Ananta, Brahma, Shiva, Indra, Ganesha, Parvati float in an ocean of joy; horses, elephants, guards, jesters, hundreds of banners; having gone round Nadia and paused on the bank of the Suradhuni, the procession approaches Mishra's house. Raga not stated. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the BR; ornate Vrajabuli.1

গৌর রসিক-শেখরবর, বেষ্টিত প্রিয় বিপ্রনিকর, হরষিত সুবিবাহ করব, ইথে চলু চঢ়ি চৌদোলে ।
তত ঘন আনদ্ধ শুষির, বাদ্য চতুর্ব্বিধ সুরুচির, বাজত বহু ভাঁতি শবদ ভরল গগন-মণ্ডলে ॥

gaura rasika-śekharabara, beṣṭita priya bipranikara, haraṣita subibāha karaba, ithe calu caṛhi caudole | tata ghana ānaddha śuṣira, bādya caturvvidha surucira, bājata bahu bhām̐ti śabada bharala gagana-maṇḍale ||

gaura — Gaura; rasika-śekhara-bara — best of the crowns of the connoisseurs of rasa; beṣṭita priya bipra-nikara — surrounded by a host of dear brahmanas; haraṣita — joyful; subibāha karaba — I shall celebrate an auspicious wedding; ithe — with this [intent]; calu caṛhi caudole — set out, mounting the palanquin; tata — strings; ghana — metal (cymbals, gongs); ānaddha — skin-covered (drums); śuṣira — winds; bādya caturvvidha surucira — splendid instruments of four kinds; bājata bahu bhām̐ti — sound in many manners; śabada bharala gagana-maṇḍale — the sound filled the vault of the sky

1.1Gaura, best of the crowns of the connoisseurs of rasa, surrounded by His dear brahmanas — "joyfully I shall celebrate an auspicious wedding!" — sets out, mounting the palanquin; strings, metal, drums and winds — splendid instruments of the four kinds — sound in many manners: the sound has filled the vault of the sky.2

সর্ব্ব বাদ্য শোভন নব, মর্দ্দল মুদবর্দ্ধন রব, ধো ধো ধিগি তগ ধিলঙ্গ, ধা ধা নি নি নিধিয়া ।
অলখিত সুর-নর্ত্তকীগণ, নর্ত্তকী সহ লাস্য সঘন, ভণ তক তক থৈ থৈ থৈ, আই অতি নি নি নি তিয়া ॥

sarvva bādya śobhana naba, marddala mudabarddhana raba, dho dho dhigi taga dhilaṅga, dhā dhā ni ni nidhiyā | alakhita sura-narttakīgaṇa, narttakī saha lāsya saghana, bhaṇa taka taka thai thai thai, āi ati ni ni ni tiyā ||

sarvva bādya śobhana naba — all the instruments splendid and new; marddala — the mardala (drum); muda-barddhana raba — a sound increasing joy; dho dho dhigi taga dhilaṅga, dhā dhā ni ni nidhiyā — onomatopoeia of the drum-strokes; alakhita — invisible; sura-narttakī-gaṇa — the celestial dancers; narttakī saha — together with the [earthly] dancers; lāsya saghana — dance the lasya without pause; bhaṇa taka taka thai thai thai, āi ati ni ni ni tiyā — the dance-count

1.2All the instruments are splendid and new; the boom of the mardala increases the joy: "dho-dho dhigi taga dhilanga, dha-dha ni-ni nidhiya"; invisible, the celestial dancers together with the [earthly] dancers dance the lasya without pause: "bhana taka-taka thai-thai-thai, ai ati ni-ni-ni tiya".

গায়কগণে মিলি উলসিত, গায়ত গন্ধর্ব্ব ললিত, শ্রুতি সুমধুর গ্রামাদি বিবিধে কৌতুক পরকাশয়ে ।
দশশত মুখ বিহি মহেশ, গণ সহ সুরপতি গণেশ, গিরিজাদিক ধৃতি কি ধরব সুখ-সায়রে ভাসয়ে ॥

gāyakagaṇe mili ulasita, gāyata gandharvva lalita, śruti sumadhura grāmādi bibidhe kautuka parakāśaye | daśaśata mukha bihi maheśa, gaṇa saha surapati gaṇeśa, girijādika dhṛti ki dharaba sukha-sāyare bhāsaye ||

gāyaka-gaṇe mili — together with the singers; ulasita — rejoicing; gāyata gandharvva lalita — the gandharvas sing sweetly; śruti — the shrutis (intervals); sumadhura grāmādi — sweet gramas and the rest; bibidhe — in many ways; kautuka parakāśaye — display their delight; daśa-śata mukha — the Thousand-mouthed [Ananta]; bihi — Brahma; maheśa — Shiva; gaṇa saha surapati — the lord of the gods [Indra] with his retinue; gaṇeśa — Ganesha; girijādika — Girija (Parvati) and others; dhṛti ki dharaba — how could they keep composure?; sukha-sāyare bhāsaye — float in an ocean of joy

1.3Together with the singers, rejoicing, the gandharvas sing sweetly; shrutis, sweet gramas and the rest — in every manner they display their delight; the Thousand-mouthed One, Brahma, Mahesha, the lord of the gods with his retinue, Ganesha, Girija and others — how could they keep their composure? — float in an ocean of joy.3

হয় গজ বহু অস্ত্রধারী, প্রকটত গুণ হাস্যকারী, লসত শত পতাকাদিক ভীড়ে পথ রোকঈ ।
নদীয়াপুর ভরমি ভরমি, সুরধুনী-তীরে বিরমি বিরমি, মিশ্রগৃহ সমীপ নরহরি শোভা অবলোকঈ ॥

haya gaja bahu astradhārī, prakaṭata guṇa hāsyakārī, lasata śata patākādika bhīṛe patha rokaī | nadīyāpura bharami bharami, suradhunī-tīre birami birami, miśragṛha samīpa narahari śobhā abalokaī ||

haya — horses; gaja — elephants; bahu astra-dhārī — many armed men; prakaṭata guṇa hāsya-kārī — the jesters display their skill; lasata śata patākādika — hundreds of banners and the like shine; bhīṛe patha rokaī — the crowd blocks the road; nadīyā-pura bharami bharami — going round the town of Nadia; suradhunī-tīre birami birami — pausing again and again on the bank of the Suradhuni (Ganga); miśra-gṛha samīpa — near Mishra's house; narahari śobhā abalokaī — Narahari beholds the splendour

1.4Horses, elephants, many armed men; jesters display their arts; hundreds of banners and the like shine — the crowd blocks the road; going round the town of Nadia, pausing again and again on the bank of the Suradhuni — near Mishra's house Narahari beholds this splendour.

(ed. 1912, pp. 809–810; ed. 1960, vv. 1495–1498), immediately after pada no. 17 on the same procession signed by Ghanashyama ("ghana ghanaśyāma hiya umatāaī"; = BR vv. 1491–1494 — outside the appendix); after it the BR gives all the wedding padas of this chapter one after another (vv. 1499–1614), then prose: Vishnupriya's service to her mother-in-law and the Lord's journey to Gaya (vv. 1615–1625). Variants: 1.1 GPT1 "surata cira" (misprint?), BR "surucira" — following the BR; 1.3 BR "surapati" — the same. Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. The wedding with Vishnupriya — CB Adi 15; CC Adi 16; Murari 1.14. energy, and the wedding with her is the Lord's lila (note 30 of chapter 21). The Lord is bound by nothing that is enjoined; He accepts the wedding rites following the lila, for the joy of His mother and His associates (note 2 of chapter 21). So are all the padas of the chapter about the Lord's "marrying" to be understood. The instruments "of the four kinds" (tata ghana ānaddha śuṣira) — strings, metal (cymbals, gongs), skin-covered (drums) and winds — are the classical division of Indian music. One"), Brahma, Shiva (Mahesha), Indra ("the lord of the gods"), Ganesha, Parvati (Girija); invisible to men, they come to serve their Lord and to behold His lila. The gandharvas are the celestial singers; shrutis and gramas are the intervals and scales of Indian music; lasya is the tender, "feminine" kind of dance.

2. Narahari — "gorācām̐dera bibāha dekhibāre…" (GPT1 p. 100, no. 19; BR)

The wives of noble families, with great longing, adorn themselves to see Gorachand's wedding: collyrium, braids with golden clasps, sindura and sandal, necklaces, flowers in their ears, silk saris; with stately gait they go to the wedding, and on seeing the poet's Lord they whisper. Raga not stated. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the BR.4

গোরাচাঁদের বিবাহ দেখিবারে ।
কত না মনের সাধে, সাজয়ে কুলের বধূ, ধৈরজ ধরিতে কেউ নারে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

gorācām̐dera bibāha dekhibāre |
kata nā manera sādhe, sājaye kulera badhū, dhairaja dharite keu nāre || dhru ||

gorācām̐dera bibāha dekhibāre — to see Gorachand's wedding; kata nā manera sādhe — with what longing of heart; sājaye kulera badhū — the wives of noble families adorn themselves; dhairaja dharite keu nāre — no one can keep her composure

2.1To see Gorachand's wedding, with what longing the wives of noble families adorn themselves — not one can keep her composure!

রসের আবেশে আঁখে, অঞ্জন রঞ্জয় কিবা, বঙ্কিম চাহনি বঙ্ক ভুরু ।
চিকণ চিকুর বেণী, পীঠেতে লোটায় কিবা, কনক-নির্ম্মিত ঝাঁপা চারু ॥

rasera ābeśe ām̐khe, añjana rañjaya kibā, baṅkima cāhani baṅka bhuru |
cikaṇa cikura beṇī, pīṭhete loṭāya kibā, kanaka-nirmmita jhām̐pā cāru ||

rasera ābeśe — absorbed in rasa; ām̐khe añjana rañjaya kibā — how charmingly they line their eyes with collyrium; baṅkima cāhani — sidelong glances; baṅka bhuru — arched brows; cikaṇa cikura beṇī — smooth braids; pīṭhete loṭāya kibā — how they fall down the back; kanaka-nirmmita jhām̐pā cāru — lovely golden clasps

2.2Absorbed in rasa, how charmingly they line their eyes with collyrium — sidelong glances, arched brows; smooth braids fall down their backs — how lovely the golden clasps!

কপালে সিন্দুর-বিন্দু, চন্দন শোভয়ে কিবা, ঝলমল করে আভরণে ।
মণি-মুকুতার মালা, গলায় দোলয়ে কিবা, গন্ধরাজ চাঁপা দেই কাণে ॥

kapāle sindura-bindu, candana śobhaye kibā, jhalamala kare ābharaṇe |
maṇi-mukutāra mālā, galāya dolaye kibā, gandharāja cām̐pā dei kāṇe ||

kapāle sindura-bindu — a dot of sindura on the forehead; candana śobhaye kibā — how beautifully the sandal shines; jhalamala kare ābharaṇe — the ornaments glitter; maṇi-mukutāra mālā — necklaces of gems and pearls; galāya dolaye kibā — how they sway on the neck; gandharāja cām̐pā — gandharaja and champaka flowers; dei kāṇe — they put in their ears

2.3On the forehead a dot of sindura, how beautifully the sandal shines! Their ornaments glitter; on their necks sway necklaces of gems and pearls; in their ears they put gandharaja and champaka flowers.

পরিয়া পাটের শাড়ী, ছাড়িয়া ভবন কিবা, চলি যায় গজেন্দ্র-গমনে ।
নরহরি-নাথে নিরখিয়া হিয়া উথলয়ে, কেউ কিছু কহে কারু কাণে ॥

pariyā pāṭera śāṛī, chāṛiyā bhabana kibā, cali yāya gajendra-gamane |
narahari-nāthe nirakhiyā hiyā uthalaye, keu kichu kahe kāru kāṇe ||

pariyā pāṭera śāṛī — putting on silk saris; chāṛiyā bhabana — leaving their homes; cali yāya gajendra-gamane — they go with the gait of a royal elephant; narahari-nāthe nirakhiyā — seeing the Lord of Narahari; hiyā uthalaye — the heart overflows; keu kichu kahe kāru kāṇe — one whispers something in another's ear

2.4Putting on silk saris, leaving their homes, they walk with a stately gait like that of a royal elephant; seeing Narahari's Lord — the heart overflows — one whispers something into another's ear.5

Variant: in 2.3 the BR has the second half-lines interchanged ("…gandharāja cām̐pā dei kāṇe" in the first line, "…jhalamala kare ābharaṇe" in the second). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Line 2.1 is the refrain (dhru). The first line is the same as that of the pada on the first wedding (2.3 no. 22, no. 7 of chapter 21), but the text is different. enamoured of Gaura. We translate faithfully to the author; but the Gaudiya tradition (Vrindavana Dasa, Krishnadasa Kaviraja, Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati) does not accept the worship of Gaura in the mood of "Gaura-nagari": Gaura is Krishna Himself in the mood and lustre of Radha; He came to taste Her love, not to enjoy as a nagara. The Lord's attractiveness for the people of Navadvipa is the quality of Bhagavan, who attracts all; it is not worldly passion. The same holds for the other padas of the chapter about the women of Nadia (nos. 3, 11, 12; cf. note 5 of chapter 21). GPT pada no. 21 ("āhā mari ki madhura rīti": the "nagaris of Nadia" dream of being "with Gora day and night" and of touching His golden body in the bridal chamber; = BR vv. 1507–1510) is openly in nagari-bhava and is assigned to the section of nagari padas.

3. Narahari — "sai ai dekha nadīyāra cām̐de…" (GPT1 p. 101, no. 20; BR)

A woman says to her friend: look at the Moon of Nadia — hundreds of Kamadevas, offering themselves for His beauty, fall weeping at His feet; His glance, His face, His smile; who has arranged this wedding attire — the crown, the curls, the yellow thread and durva, the golden mirror? Raga not stated. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the BR.6

সই অই দেখ নদীয়ার চাঁদে ।
ভুবনমোহন ও না রূপের নিছনি লৈঞা, কত শত মদন চরণে পড়ি কাঁদে ॥ ধ্রু ॥

sai ai dekha nadīyāra cām̐de |
bhubanamohana o nā rūpera nichani laiñā, kata śata madana caraṇe paṛi kām̐de || dhru ||

sai — friend; ai dekha nadīyāra cām̐de — look, there is the Moon of Nadia; bhubana-mohana — world-enchanting; o nā rūpera nichani laiñā — offering themselves for that beauty; kata śata madana — hundreds upon hundreds of Madanas; caraṇe paṛi kām̐de — fall at His feet and weep

3.1Friend, look — there is the Moon of Nadia! Offering themselves for His world-enchanting beauty, hundreds upon hundreds of Madanas fall weeping at His feet.

রসে ডুবু ডুবু দুটী নয়ান-চাহনি, বিধি সিরজিল যুবতী বধিতে হেন বাসি ।
বদন-চাঁদের শোভা, চাঁদের গরব হরে, হাসি মিশে অমিয়া বরষে রাশি রাশি ॥

rase ḍubu ḍubu duṭī nayāna-cāhani, bidhi sirajila yubatī badhite hena bāsi |
badana-cām̐dera śobhā, cām̐dera garaba hare, hāsi miśe amiyā baraṣe rāśi rāśi ||

rase ḍubu ḍubu — drowning in rasa; duṭī nayāna-cāhani — the glance of the two eyes; bidhi sirajila — the Creator made; yubatī badhite — to slay young women; hena bāsi — so I think; badana-cām̐dera śobhā — the beauty of the moon-face; cām̐dera garaba hare — takes away the moon's pride; hāsi miśe — mingled with the smile; amiyā baraṣe rāśi rāśi — nectar pours down in heaps

3.2The glance of His two eyes, drowning in rasa — I think the Creator made it to slay young women; the beauty of His moon-face takes away the moon's pride; mingled with His smile, nectar pours down in streams.7

আহা মরি মরি যেন কত না মনের সাধে, কেবা বনাইল এ না বিবাহের বেশ ।
পরম উজ্জ্বল অতি বিচিত্র মুকুট মাথে, ঝাঁপিয়াছে চিকণ চাঁচর চারু কেশ ॥

āhā mari mari yena kata nā manera sādhe, kebā banāila e nā bibāhera beśa |
parama ujjvala ati bicitra mukuṭa māthe, jhām̐piyāche cikaṇa cām̐cara cāru keśa ||

āhā mari mari — ah, I die, I die; yena kata nā manera sādhe — as if with what longing of heart; kebā banāila — who has arranged; e nā bibāhera beśa — this wedding attire; parama ujjvala ati bicitra mukuṭa māthe — on His head a wondrous, dazzlingly bright crown; jhām̐piyāche — have covered; cikaṇa cām̐cara cāru keśa — smooth, curling, lovely locks

3.3Ah, I die, I die! With what longing of heart has someone arranged this wedding attire! On His head a wondrous, dazzlingly bright crown, covered by His smooth, curling, lovely locks.

মঙ্গল-বিহিত পীতসূতা দূর্ব্বাদল করে, নিরুপম কনক-দর্পণ ভাল শোহে ।
পরিধেয় বসন ভূষণ সুমধুর, প্রতি অঙ্গের ভঙ্গীতে নরহরি-মন মোহে ॥

maṅgala-bihita pītasūtā dūrvvādala kare, nirupama kanaka-darpaṇa bhāla śohe |
paridheya basana bhūṣaṇa sumadhura, prati aṅgera bhaṅgīte narahari-mana mohe ||

maṅgala-bihita — enjoined for the auspicious rite; pīta-sūtā — the yellow thread; dūrvvā-dala kare — blades of durva in the hand; nirupama kanaka-darpaṇa — the incomparable golden mirror; bhāla śohe — shines beautifully; paridheya basana bhūṣaṇa sumadhura — the garments and ornaments are sweet; prati aṅgera bhaṅgīte — by the grace of every limb; narahari-mana mohe — enchants Narahari's mind

3.4In His hand the yellow thread and the blades of durva enjoined for the auspicious rite; the incomparable golden mirror shines beautifully; His garments and ornaments are sweet; by the grace of every limb [He] enchants Narahari's mind.

The variants are minor (3.1 GPT1 "laiñā", BR "laiyā"; 3.3 GPT1 "enā", BR "e nā"). Not in PK, KGC, PS, the Gita-chandrodaya or the Gaura-charita-chintamani. B. Line 3.1 is the refrain. The next pada in the GPT and the BR (no. 21) is in nagari-bhava (note 5). beauty of the Lord (see note 5). Madana is Kamadeva, the god of love; hundreds of Madanas "offer themselves" (nichani — give themselves as a ransom) for His beauty: it surpasses the beauty of Kamadeva himself.

4. Narahari — "sanātana miśrera bhabane…" (GPT1 pp. 101–102, no. 22; BR)
